mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) over the past month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the past month indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where UNRATE decreases by > 0.2pp in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past two months signals a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances where HOUST increases over the previous two months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past month signals a weakening supply side, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to concerns about economic slowdown.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases by > 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the past month, it signals a tightening monetary policy in response to inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases over the past month, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the past month signals strong consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances where RSAFS increases by > 1% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is negative over the past quarter, it signals an accommodative monetary policy in response to economic contraction, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as markets anticipate recovery.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% and GDPC1 growth < 0% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 1% and GDPC1 growth is negative in the previous quarter.
